Alert expression (PromQL): label_replace(label_replace((sum by (k8s_namespace_name, service_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{k8s_namespace_name="otel-demo",service_name="checkout",span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER",span_name=~".*CheckoutService/PlaceOrder",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}[5m]))) / (sum by (k8s_namespace_name, service_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{k8s_namespace_name="otel-demo",service_name="checkout",span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER",span_name=~".*CheckoutService/PlaceOrder"}[5m]))), "namespace", "$1", "k8s_namespace_name", "(.*)"), "service", "$1", "service_name", "(.*)") > 0.5
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The alert is real: at 2026-11-14T19:52:54Z checkout's oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder server spans had error rate 0.03615202563344014/s and STATUS_CODE_UNSET rate 0, i.e. a 100% error ratio. Every failing PlaceOrder fails on its outbound oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge call, and the payment service's own server span grpc.oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge is what throws 'Payment request failed. Invalid token. app.loyalty.level=gold' at /usr/src/app/charge.js:37. The deepest supported cause is the flagd feature flag paymentFailure ('Fail payment service charge requests n%'), whose current flagd-config content has state ENABLED and defaultVariant '100%' (variant value 1), so payment rejects 100% of charge requests by design. This is a configuration-only change: no pod restarted, all images are unchanged 2.0.2/v0.12.8, and the flagd pod logged fsnotify CHMOD then REMOVE events on etc/flagd/demo.flagd.json at 19:47:34.637Z — 21s before payment's first logged failure at 19:47:55Z and about 5 minutes before the alert fired. Payment's logs show 'Transaction complete' successes through 19:46:53Z and every charge failing thereafter, including requests reusing card numbers that had previously succeeded, which argues against bad card input. The change_history integration is not available, so who or what rewrote the flag, and its previous variant, cannot be verified.

claims.text: At the alert evaluation time 2026-11-14T19:52:54Z, checkout's oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder server spans showed rate 0.03615202563344014 with status_code STATUS_CODE_ERROR and rate 0 with status_code STATUS_CODE_UNSET, i.e. a 100% error ratio, satisfying the alert threshold (> 0.5).

From 18:53:04Z through roughly 19:49Z the PlaceOrder STATUS_CODE_UNSET rate for checkout was non-zero (peaking near 0.033/s) and no STATUS_CODE_ERROR series appeared in the sampled points; the ERROR series is present from the 19:50:04Z point onward, and the UNSET rate drops to 0 at the 19:52:04Z and 19:53:04Z points.

At 19:52:54Z the only error-status checkout spans were oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder (SPAN_KIND_SERVER, 0.03615202563344014/s) and its client span oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge (SPAN_KIND_CLIENT, 0.03615202563344014/s), at identical rates; no other checkout operation had error spans, so the failure is localized to the Charge dependency call.

Sampled checkout error spans carry otel.status_description 'failed to charge card: could not charge the card: rpc error: code = Unknown desc = Payment request failed. Invalid token. app.loyalty.level=gold' (rpc.grpc.status_code 13), and the child span oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge on the same traces carries 'Payment request failed. Invalid token. app.loyalty.level=gold' (rpc.grpc.status_code 2), each Charge span being a CHILD_OF a failing PlaceOrder span.

The payment service's own server span grpc.oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge errors with grpc.error_message and exception.message 'Payment request failed. Invalid token. app.loyalty.level=gold', with stacktrace 'Error: Payment request failed. Invalid token. ... at module.exports.charge (/usr/src/app/charge.js:37:13) at async Object.chargeServiceHandler [as charge] (/usr/src/app/index.js:21:22)'; its nested internal 'charge' span is present but not_recorded.

Payment's own grpc.oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge server-span metrics show the same transition: STATUS_CODE_ERROR rate 0.013246 at 19:50:04Z, 0.009956 at 19:51:04Z, 0.022150 at 19:52:04Z, 0.037402 at 19:53:04Z, while STATUS_CODE_UNSET for that span falls to 0.004167, 0 and 0 at the last points (previously up to 0.033/s).

Payment pod payment-6f7bc865d6-9md52 logged successful charges ('msg":"Transaction complete."') at 19:40:16Z, 19:40:24Z, 19:41:15Z, 19:41:33Z, 19:42:53Z, 19:42:59Z, 19:43:33Z, 19:44:21Z, 19:44:29Z, 19:44:52Z, 19:45:03Z, 19:45:28Z and 19:46:53Z, then level=warn 'Payment request failed. Invalid token. app.loyalty.level=gold' (charge.js:37:13) for every later charge at 19:47:55Z, 19:48:03Z, 19:50:18Z, 19:50:20Z, 19:50:52Z, 19:51:08Z, 19:51:20Z, 19:51:29Z, 19:51:49Z, 19:52:12Z, 19:52:34Z and 19:53:02Z.

The flagd ConfigMap flagd-config defines flag paymentFailure with description 'Fail payment service charge requests n%', state ENABLED, variants {'100%':1,'90%':0.95,'75%':0.75,'50%':0.5,'25%':0.25,'10%':0.1,'off':0} and defaultVariant '100%'; every other flag in the same file (productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure, adManualGc, adHighCpu, adFailure, kafkaQueueProblems, cartFailure, paymentUnreachable, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage, imageSlowLoad) has defaultVariant 'off'.

The flagd pod flagd-d6485586b-6ppgj logged at 2026-11-14T19:47:34.637Z two fsnotify events on 'etc/flagd/demo.flagd.json': 'filepath event: etc/flagd/demo.flagd.json CHMOD' then 'REMOVE' (component sync, sync fsnotify) — the file-replacement pattern a mounted ConfigMap update produces; these are the only flagd log lines in 19:30:00Z-19:53:04Z.

Payment is the only service with flagd evaluation spans: over 19:03:04Z-19:53:04Z exactly one such series exists, service_name=payment, span_name=grpc.flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/ResolveFloat (a float/percentage-style flag), with rate 0.004155781 at the 19:53:04Z point only, i.e. its evaluation activity appears in the incident's final 5-minute bucket.

No workload was restarted or replaced: payment-6f7bc865d6-9md52, checkout-6578865d87-sk69g and flagd-d6485586b-6ppgj are Running with restartCount 0 and startTime 2026-11-14T16:32:3xZ, and the payment, checkout and flagd deployments each report 1 ready, 1 available, 1 updated with unchanged images ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.0.2-payment, ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.0.2-checkout and ghcr.io/open-feature/flagd:v0.12.8.

The only Kubernetes events in the otel-demo namespace inside the authorized window concern a Prometheus/Alertmanager/prometheus-readonly-proxy pod replacement at 19:29:02Z-19:29:08Z; no events reference payment, checkout, flagd or the flagd-config ConfigMap.

In the sampled failing traces checkout's other dependencies returned success: checkout's oteldemo.CartService/GetCart, oteldemo.CurrencyService/Convert, oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct and oteldemo.ShippingService/GetQuote client spans all show rpc.grpc.status_code=0 with error_rows 0, and the corresponding cart, currency, product-catalog, shipping and quote spans show rpc.grpc.status_code=0, http.status_code 200, or not_recorded with 0 error rows.

In the same sampled traces the callers above checkout recorded their own HTTP 500 errors: frontend 'POST /api/checkout' (http.status_code 500), frontend 'executing api route (pages) /api/checkout' and frontend 'POST' (error, http 500), frontend-proxy 'ingress' and 'router frontend egress' (http 500), and load-generator 'POST' (http 500), all inside traces whose checkout PlaceOrder span failed. This is a biased 3-trace sample, not a failure count.

Deepest supported cause: the flagd flag paymentFailure is served at its 100% variant (value 1, 'Fail payment service charge requests n%'), so the payment service deterministically throws 'Payment request failed. Invalid token. app.loyalty.level=gold' from charge.js:37 for every charge, checkout's PlaceOrder fails on that call, and the alert fires. paymentFailure's numeric variants match payment's grpc.flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/ResolveFloat evaluations, and the observed total (not partial) charge failure fits the '100%' variant rather than 90/75/50/25/10%.

The flag took effect through a configuration-only change at 19:47:34Z: flagd's fsnotify CHMOD and REMOVE events on etc/flagd/demo.flagd.json at 19:47:34.637Z match a mounted flagd-config ConfigMap rewrite, and payment's first failure followed 21s later at 19:47:55Z with no restart, no new image and no ReplicaSet change. The ConfigMap creationTimestamp (16:32:37Z) does not change on data updates, so it cannot date the content change.

Rejected: invalid card/token data from callers caused the rejections. The same card numbers succeeded before the onset and failed after it (4929-5431-0337-5647 completed at 19:40:16Z, 19:42:59Z, 19:44:29Z and 19:45:28Z but failed at 19:50:18Z), the throw originates at the fixed charge.js:37 site rather than a card-validation branch, and the failure text is identical ('app.loyalty.level=gold') for requests whose logged loyalty levels were bronze, silver, gold and platinum.

Rejected: payment was unreachable, crashed or overloaded. Payment answered every charge with a sub-millisecond application-level gRPC error (grpc.oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge spans 702-798us plus internal 'charge' spans 221-242us), the pod is Running with 0 restarts and the deployment 1/1 ready, the paymentUnreachable flag is 'off', and payment's flagd client spans carry no error — so this is a deliberate application rejection, not a transport failure.

Counter-evidence against a checkout-side defect: checkout's error spans are confined to PlaceOrder and its PaymentService/Charge client span at identical rates, checkout's other dependency calls in the sampled traces all returned rpc.grpc.status_code=0, and no K8s event or restart touched checkout — so checkout is propagating payment's rejection rather than originating a failure of its own.

Advisory (not executed): inspect the flagd-config ConfigMap change/audit trail or the controller that writes it to identify what set paymentFailure defaultVariant to '100%' at ~19:47:34Z, and restore it to 'off'; the flag value is the only runtime-tunable input that matches the onset, and no pod action is needed because flagd reloads the mounted file.
